label: Open
summary: Open a file, app bundle or folder as the active target. Detects what it is from its contents. For raw machine code pass format=raw-binary with architecture and entry_point.

label: Close
summary: Close the active target (or the one named). Evidence stays in the project.

label: Session status
summary: What's open, which target is active, Clean room or Deep mode, evidence and unknown counts, version.

label: List open targets
summary: Every open target with its id, kind and sha256.

label: Switch target
summary: Make another open target the active one.

label: Where am I
summary: The current cursor address in the active target.

label: Evidence so far
summary: All evidence recorded in this session (detail=summary for a compact list; filter by operation or evidence_id).

label: Export evidence
summary: Write every evidence record and unknown to a JSON bundle file.

label: Import evidence
summary: Load a bundle written by core_evidence_export. Tampered records are rejected.

label: Open questions
summary: Recorded unknowns, filtered by status, severity or domain.

label: Record an open question
summary: Record something not yet known, with what would settle it.

label: Update an open question
summary: Change an unknown's status, evidence or resolution. Pass based_on_revision; a stale revision gives stale_revision.

label: Check an answer
summary: Check that a resolved unknown has a resolution and cites evidence that exists and is intact.

label: Inventory an archive or app bundle
summary: Content-addressed inventory of a ZIP/APK/IPA/JAR, Electron ASAR, app bundle or folder: every file with size, kind, role and sha256; nested archives opened to a bounded depth; ASAR integrity hashes and ZIP CRCs checked. Paged (offset/limit).

label: Extract an archive
summary: Extract every regular file of a ZIP/APK/IPA/JAR or ASAR (plus its .asar.unpacked files) into a fresh private temporary folder chosen by Craft Anything, and return its path. Bounded size and count; entries that would escape the folder are refused.

label: Compare two artifacts
summary: Compare two archives, app bundles or folders file by file: added, removed, changed (by sha256) and moved files. Inputs are absolute paths or core_archive_show evidence.

label: Analyse a JavaScript app
summary: Static analysis of an Electron app (app.asar or unpacked folder), a web bundle folder, a ZIP or a single script into an application graph: package and entry points (main, preload, renderer), BrowserWindow webPreferences, the IPC channel map (ipcMain.handle/on ↔ ipcRenderer.invoke/send, contextBridge members), module imports, bundler and chunk splitting (webpack, esbuild, browserify; Vite/Rollup de

label: Match static code to what ran
summary: Match app graph evidence against what was seen running (captured scripts with URLs and sha256): each static module is loaded, resident in a loaded bundle, loaded with different content, not observed, or unknown; runtime-only scripts are listed. Pure computation over evidence.

label: Export captured scripts
summary: Write the scripts held by a web capture (page inspection or walkthrough evidence, a capture JSON file, or a HAR with saved bodies) into a new folder as files/<host>/<path> plus manifest.json; query variants and collisions get content-hash names with a stated reason. The result names the folder to pass to js_app_map.

label: Find the original source line
summary: Map a position in generated (bundled/minified) JavaScript back to its original file, line, column and name through a source map (a .map file, a script's sourceMappingURL, or an inline data: map). Lines are 1-based, columns 0-based UTF-16. Returns every original position at that point and nearby original source when the map embeds it.

label: Inspect a network recording
summary: Read a HAR capture offline: requests, methods, statuses, hosts, timings and an API surface grouped by method + origin + path template, with JSON bodies reduced to outlines (no values). Cookies, credential headers, URL user-info and credential-like query values are never kept; secrets the caller names are redacted in raw, URL-encoded and JSON-escaped forms. Paged (offset/limit) or pick entries with

label: Recover readable sources
summary: Turn minified bundles back into readable files in a new folder: split webpack/esbuild/browserify module tables into one file per module, pretty-print everything, apply safe unminify rewrites (!0→true, void 0→undefined, statement sequences, webpack module parameter names via scope analysis) and write original files embedded in source maps. manifest.json records every input digest, module byte range

label: Connect to a browser
summary: Attach to a loopback CDP endpoint (a browser started with --remote-debugging-port) or launch a located Chromium headless, and report the product, protocol version and debuggable target count. A quick connectivity check before the other browser tools.

label: List browser pages
summary: List the debuggable targets (pages, workers, iframes) of a loopback CDP endpoint with their ids, kinds and origin-only URLs, plus the browser product and protocol version. Read-only discovery over HTTP; no WebSocket.

label: Inspect a web page
summary: Passively observe one page over CDP for a short window: frame origins, a DOM summary (node names/types and attribute names with value lengths only), parsed scripts (optionally their sources, each with its sha256), resources, and — each opt-in — accessibility names, console entries, network request outlines, WebSocket outlines and storage key names. Never navigates, clicks or evaluates. Cookies, au

label: Analyse a page's JavaScript
summary: Fetch the scripts a live page has loaded over CDP and run the built-in JavaScript analyser on them: chunk graph, module boundaries, routes, HTTP endpoints and vendor fingerprints. Optionally decodes inline (data:) source maps and fetches same-origin maps. Passive; nothing is executed.

label: Watch a page over time
summary: Passively watch one page over a longer window (default 10s) and record a bounded timeline of network request outlines, console entries, WebSocket frame outlines and navigation/lifecycle events, all data-minimised. Never navigates or evaluates.

label: Find in-page MCP tools
summary: Best effort: enable the experimental WebMCP CDP domain and collect any tools the page advertises (names and declared input outlines only) during a short window. The tools are never invoked. Honest when the browser does not support the domain.

label: Screenshot a page
summary: Capture a PNG screenshot of the current state of one page and return it inline with its sha256 (plus bytes, dimensions, base64). Passive; the page is not navigated.

label: Compare two page captures
summary: Compare two web_page_show captures (frame origins, elements, resources, endpoints and script URLs added or removed), or two web_walkthrough_record runs step by step (steps aligned by step_id, then position: action, status, URL, error and artifact changes; network requests; event counts). normalization lists plain text replacements (e.g. a build id) applied to both sides first. Pure computation ove

label: Compare two screenshots
summary: Compare two PNG screenshots pixel by pixel with a per-channel threshold (0..255): whether they are comparable, how many pixels differ, the difference fraction, the largest channel delta and the changed bounding box. No pixel data is returned. Pure computation.

label: Run a scripted web session
summary: Run a scripted browser session (goto/click/fill/press/select/wait; elements by CSS selector, test_id, or role and accessible name; optional step_id per step) over CDP, attaching to a loopback endpoint or launching a located Chromium. A fixed environment (viewport, locale, time zone, colour scheme, reduced motion, service workers; 1280x720, en-US, UTC, light by default) makes runs repeatable. Captu

label: Check a scripted web session
summary: Check a script for web_walkthrough_record without running a browser, and list every problem with the step it's in: unknown step kinds, missing fields, selectors CSS doesn't have (XPath, :has-text and the like), locators that aren't exactly one of selector, test_id or role with name, bad settings. Errors are what the recorder would refuse, by the same rules; warnings are what it would run but proba

label: Open a website
summary: Load a web page (http/https) in a private browser owned by this session (fresh profile, no history or logins) at a chosen window size, wait for it to finish loading, and report its final address, title and size. Every browser tool then inspects this page unless given another endpoint. Runs the site's scripts, so it needs your approval.

label: Capture a website for rebuilding
summary: Record the open website into a new folder: full-page PNG screenshots at each requested width, the rendered HTML, design tokens (fonts, sizes, weights, text and background colours as hex, radii, shadows, spacing, content widths, CSS custom properties), the widths its CSS switches layout at, the layout at each width (page width, heading and text sizes, each section's padding, gap, content column and

label: Capture menus, dialogs and tabs
summary: On the open website, open up to max_states of its visible menus, pop-ups, tabs and collapsed sections (aria-expanded, aria-haspopup, unselected tabs, <summary>; never form controls or submit buttons) one at a time: click it, take a screenshot, record what changed (expanded, a dialog appeared, the tab or the address changed), then put the page back. Writes state-<n>.png and states.json into a new f

label: Close the website
summary: Close the private browser started by web_site_open and delete its temporary profile.

label: Build a stand-in backend
summary: Read a network recording (.har) of the original site and write standin.json into a folder: its routes (method and path template, with ids as {id}), and for each the status codes, content types, query names and a bounded set of recorded answers. It's for giving a rebuilt front end something to talk to. Credential headers, cookies and secret-shaped values are dropped and counted; pages, scripts and

label: Start a stand-in backend
summary: Answer HTTP requests on this computer from a file written by web_standin_build, and return its URL to point a rebuilt front end at. Listens on 127.0.0.1 only, refuses requests addressed to any other host and pages from other computers, and allows local pages through CORS. Stays running for this session, or until web_standin_stop. A request with no recorded answer gets a 404 with the nearest routes

label: Stop a stand-in backend
summary: Stop a stand-in started by web_standin_start and free its port: by id, or all of them. With neither, stops the only one running. Returns what it answered.

label: See what a stand-in was asked
summary: List the stand-ins running in this session with the requests they answered, and page through the requests that had no recorded answer, most asked first, each with why and the nearest recorded routes. This is how a builder finds out what its front end needs that the recording doesn't have.

label: Ask the person
summary: Ask the person a question in the app and wait for the answer: a short question, up to six suggested answers shown as buttons, and optionally a typed reply. Use it when a choice changes the result (scope, style, which feature first) and you can't decide from the evidence. Returns the answer text, or a note to continue with your best judgement if nobody answers within 30 minutes.

label: Approve an agent action
summary: Permission check for a coding agent's action (tool name and input). Edits inside the workspace's app folder and common build commands are allowed; dev servers are refused with a hint; anything else asks the person. Returns {behavior: allow, updatedInput} or {behavior: deny, message}.

label: List projects
summary: List the projects in every project folder from settings (where new projects go, then `project_folders`), or in one folder, newest first: name, folder, app folder, request, target, stack, status, the latest check and how many questions are waiting.

label: Show a project
summary: One project: its request, target, stack, status, checks, questions still waiting for an answer, and its conversation (paged with offset/limit, newest last).

label: Answer a project's question
summary: Answer a question or approval a project is waiting on (an id from project_show): a choice or text for questions, allow (and always) for approvals. The answer reaches a running build at once and is kept in the project's conversation.

label: Play a project's result
summary: Start the finished game or app a project built (its program, a Unity or Unreal package, or a Godot project in Godot), in its own window. If it's already running, says so instead of starting a second copy, unless `another` is true. A start that quits within two seconds is reported with its exit code and last output. It runs the code the builder wrote, so it needs the person's consent. Websites use

label: Preview a project's website
summary: Serve a project's built website on this computer only (loopback) and return its address. It keeps serving for this session; with `wait`, the call itself serves until it's cancelled (Ctrl+C in the CLI).

label: Open a project's folder
summary: Open the project's folder (or its app/ folder) in the file manager.

label: Rename a project
summary: Give a project a new name (its folder stays where it is).

label: Duplicate a project
summary: Copy a project beside it under a new name, to try something else from where it is: what was built, the pictures of the original and the study come along; the conversation, questions and usage don't, and neither do dependencies or compiler output (the next build makes them again). An app edited in place is copied into the copy's app/ folder.

label: Delete a project
summary: Delete a project: everything Craft Anything made in its folder (its records, checks, and what was built in app/). The person's own files stay (an app edited in place, the files a project started from). Can't be undone, so `confirm` must be true; stop a build first.

label: Choose what the builder's questions get
summary: Choose whether the builder's questions (core_person_ask) in a project are shown to the person to answer (`ask`) or answered with "decide yourself and say what you chose" (`decide`); `default` follows the app's setting (`questions` in settings, which follows Auto mode until set). With no mode, says what applies now. Takes effect from the builder's next question, also mid-build.

label: Call the build done
summary: The person is happy with the build as it is (#210): its status becomes Ready and the conversation says they called it done, so a paused, stopped or failed build no longer offers to carry on. Everything so far is kept, and a new message carries on from here. It doesn't stop a build that is still running: pause it first.

label: Set a project's asset budget
summary: Set what a project may spend on generated pictures and 3D models (US dollars), or read it with no amount. Shows what's been spent so far.

label: Let a project generate assets
summary: Turn on or off whether the builder may generate pictures and 3D models for a project (paid per asset from its asset budget, and only with an asset provider's key), or read it with no value. Off until the person turns it on.

label: Pin a project's build
summary: Keep the project's current build at hand to open later, whatever the builder changes next. `frozen` (the default) copies the app's files and its program into the project's pinned/ folder, without compiler output or dependencies it doesn't start from, so rebuilds can't change or break it. `light` copies the program and the code too but hard-links dependencies and media to the project's, saving thei

label: List pinned builds
summary: The pins of one project, or of every project in the project folders from settings: id, name, frozen or light, the round it was pinned at, its size, and whether it's running (started in this session).

label: Open a pinned build
summary: Start a pinned build in its own window. If it's already running, says so instead of starting a second copy, unless `another` is true (copies of one pin share the files they save beside themselves). A start that quits within two seconds is reported with its exit code and last output. It runs the code the builder wrote, so it needs the person's consent.

label: Stop a pinned build
summary: Close what a pin started in this session (every copy of it).

label: Rename a pinned build
summary: Give a pin a new name.

label: Remove a pinned build
summary: Remove a pin. Its copy goes with it, including anything the program saved beside itself there, so `confirm` must be true; a running pin is refused until it's stopped.

label: List engines
summary: What's on this computer: each external engine (where it was found, what it's for, whether it can be installed for you), Ghidra for Deep mode, and the game engines that can build games (Unity, Unreal, Godot, Rust) with whether each is ready.

label: Install an engine
summary: Download and install an engine into Craft Anything's own folder: `ghidra` (Deep mode, with its Java), `godot`, or any engine with a pinned download (`adb`, `jadx`…). Every download is checked against its published SHA-256. Unity and Unreal need their vendors' installers and accounts: on Windows the installer (Unity Hub, the Epic Games Launcher) is downloaded, its publisher checked, and opened for

label: Show settings
summary: The current settings as JSON (mode, Auto mode, Deep mode/Ghidra, engine paths, projects folder, asset budget and picture model, AI backends). API keys are never in settings.

label: Change a setting
summary: Set one setting by its dotted key from settings_show (`auto_mode`, `deep_mode`, `projects_dir`, `assets.budget_usd`…) to a JSON value, then save. Unknown keys and values of the wrong type are refused, and nothing is written.

label: List plugins
summary: The external MCP servers configured as plugins ([[plugins.mcp]] in config.toml): id, command, whether it's on and asks before each call, and the tools cached from its last refresh.

label: Refresh plugins
summary: Start a plugin's MCP server (or every enabled one), read its tool list and cache it. New or changed tools are offered from the next start of the app or CLI. It runs the plugin's program, so it needs consent.

label: Add a plugin
summary: Add an external MCP server as a plugin ([[plugins.mcp]] in config.toml): an id, and either a command (a local server, with args, env and cwd) or a url (a remote https server, with headers). A plugin added here always asks before each call. replace overwrites a plugin with the same id. Run plugins_refresh next to read its tools.

label: Remove a plugin
summary: Remove a plugin from config.toml by its id. Its tools stop being offered from the next start.

label: Open an engine's app
summary: Open Unity Hub or the Epic Games Launcher (to sign in and install the Unity Editor or Unreal Engine), found on this computer. Only those two; nothing else is started.

label: List project files
summary: List files and folders in the project being built (default: app/), a few levels deep. Paths are relative to the project folder; build output and dependencies (node_modules, target, dist…) are skipped.

label: Read a project file
summary: Read a text file in the project (app/, capture/, reference/…), paged by lines with offset/limit for big files.

label: Write a project file
summary: Create or replace a text file. Inside app/ this goes ahead; anywhere else asks the person.

label: Edit a project file
summary: Replace exact text in a file: old_text must appear exactly once (or set replace_all). Inside app/ this goes ahead; anywhere else asks the person.

label: Update the checklist
summary: Show the person your plan as a short checklist and keep it current: todos with content (a plain step), activeForm ("Drawing the map") and status (pending, in_progress or completed). Call it again whenever a step changes; the app pins it above the prompt box.

label: Run a build command
summary: Run a command in app/ (npm install, npm run build, cargo build, the game engine's build…) and return its exit code and the end of its output. Common build commands go ahead; dev servers and watchers are refused (they never exit); anything else asks the person. Default limit 10 minutes, at most 2 hours.

label: Picture a program's window
summary: Start a program (an app or a game), wait for its window, take a picture of it and close the program (Windows and macOS). Optionally save the PNG to `output`, and the UI tree of its windows (as runtime_ui_read reads it; Windows and macOS) to `ui_tree` as JSON. It runs the program, so it needs consent.

label: Generate a picture
summary: Make a picture with fal.ai (Nano Banana Pro) and save it as a PNG inside app/: a texture, a sky or background, an icon, a title screen or concept art. shape: square (1024x1024, default), wide (1024x576) or tall (576x1024). Costs about $0.15, counted against the project's asset budget. Describe original designs in the original's style; never ask for recognisable characters, logos or brand artwork.

label: Generate a 3D model
summary: Make a game-ready, low-poly 3D model (GLB) with fal.ai (Tripo P1) and save it inside app/. Give a prompt (a picture is made first, then turned into the model) or an image (a web address, or a picture inside the project such as reference/picture-1.png). faces caps the face count (48 to 20000, default 3000): about 500-1500 for small props and pickups, 2000-5000 for weapons, furniture and vehicles, 6

label: List Electron pages
summary: List the debuggable targets of an Electron app started with --remote-debugging-port (loopback), labelling renderer pages (file:// or app:// URLs) and other targets. Attach-only discovery over HTTP.

label: Inspect an Electron page
summary: Passively inspect one Electron renderer page (a hostless file:// page) over CDP: frame origins, a DOM summary, parsed scripts (optionally their sources) and, opt-in, console entries. Never navigates or evaluates; values are never kept.

label: Run a scripted Electron session
summary: Launch an Electron app's own executable with a private profile and a loopback debugging port, run a short script (wait / reload / navigate / click) against its first renderer, capture network request outlines, then terminate the owned process. Executes the app and accesses the network, so it needs your approval.

label: List JS runtime targets
summary: List the inspectable targets of a Node or Electron process started with --inspect (loopback V8 inspector endpoint), with their ids and whether another client is attached. Attach-only discovery.

label: Observe a JS runtime
summary: Attach the V8 inspector to one Node/Electron target and observe passively: it sends exactly Runtime.enable and Debugger.enable, then records the scripts parsed (deduplicated and sorted), execution contexts and a parse-failure count. Never resumes a paused (--inspect-brk) target. runtime_kind is taken as given.

label: Measure which code ran
summary: Turn on V8 precise coverage on one page, observe for a window, then report per-script which functions and block ranges ran (UTF-16 offsets, with call counts when available). Changes the page's profiler state and discards coverage data on stop, so it is not idempotent.

label: List a node's event listeners
summary: Resolve a CSS selector on one page and list the DOM event listeners registered on that element: event type, capture/passive/once flags and the handler's script location (URL, line, column). No handler source is read.

label: Map a page's module graph
summary: Fetch the scripts a live page has loaded and build their ES module import graph: each script and the specifiers it imports, resolved to URLs where relative, with bare specifiers reported as needing an import map. Static reading of the live sources; nothing is executed.

label: Trace a feature
summary: Follow a feature through an application graph from a seed (module, function, string, IPC channel, endpoint, route, bridge API or node id): what leads to it and what it leads to, across renderer ↔ preload ↔ main, with readable chains and a one-line story.

label: Explain a function
summary: Function-level slice of an application graph: for the seeded functions, their calls (resolved where possible), callers (resolved or same-name inferred), strings, the IPC/effects/endpoints/storage they touch, and a depth-limited callee tree. Unresolved dynamic calls are listed.

label: Compare two app versions
summary: Compare two application graphs: modules (unchanged, changed, moved by content, renamed by structure, added, removed), bundle modules (content → structure → id), IPC channels and handlers, bridge members, endpoints, routes, window webPreferences, native modules and vendor versions.

label: Compare module exports
summary: Compare what each module exports (ES module names, CommonJS names, the kind of module.exports) between two application graphs, matching modules by path then by structure.

label: Import a source folder
summary: Read a reference source tree (honouring .gitignore, skipping .git and hidden files) into a source graph: every file with sha256 and language; JavaScript/TypeScript files with exports, imports, function names, strings and a structural fingerprint. Use with js_source_bundle_compare.

label: Line up source with the bundle
summary: Match reference source files (from app_source_import, or a folder path) to the shipped app's files and bundle modules by path, source-map listing, shared strings, function names and export names; reports matches with scores and reasons, unmatched sources and bundle code without a source.

label: Build a rebuild ledger
summary: Derive the expectations a clean-room rebuild must meet from an application graph (IPC handlers, bridge members, windows, endpoints, routes, storage, file/process effects, native modules, entry point) and mark each one proven only when the manifest gives it one owner, a parser type where needed, every case it must cover with strong enough evidence, and a passing check with its result. Ledger status

label: How complete is the rebuild
summary: Summarise a rebuild ledger: the share of in-scope expectations proven, counts by layer and status, and the open gaps with what each still needs.

label: Map an Android app
summary: Project an Android package's inventory (core_archive_show evidence or a path) into an application graph: manifest, DEX code, native libraries by ABI, split APKs, signing files, resources and embedded runtimes (Flutter, React Native/Hermes, Cordova/Capacitor, .NET, Unity…). Runtime hints are inferred from file names.

label: Map an Apple app
summary: Project an iOS/macOS app's inventory (core_archive_show evidence or a path) into an application graph: bundles and extensions, executables, frameworks, dylibs, signing material, interface files, asset catalogs and embedded runtimes (Flutter, React Native, Electron, Unity…). Runtime hints are inferred from file names.

label: Map a HarmonyOS app
summary: Project a HarmonyOS package's inventory (core_archive_show evidence or a path) into an application graph: module manifests, HAP/HSP packages, Ark bytecode, native libraries by ABI and resources.

label: Investigation so far
summary: The working memory of this investigation: brief, plan with step status, hypotheses, findings (with evidence ids) and the latest handoff. Read it first when starting or resuming.

label: Write the brief
summary: Set the investigation brief: the question, purpose, targets, constraints and what 'done' means. Write it before the first analysis call on a new question.

label: Update the plan
summary: Replace the plan with a numbered list of steps, each todo/doing/done/blocked with a short why. Pass based_on_revision to avoid overwriting someone else's update.

label: Record a hypothesis
summary: Record a claim being tested, ideally with the prediction that would confirm or refute it, plus any supporting/contradicting evidence ids.

label: Update a hypothesis
summary: Change a hypothesis's status (testing/supported/refuted/abandoned) and attach supporting or contradicting evidence ids and notes.

label: Record a finding
summary: Record a settled answer. Requires at least one evidence id; every id is checked against the ledger. Findings are the source for reports.

label: Write the handoff
summary: Rewrite the handoff note: where we are, what's next, traps to avoid. Write it at the end of every turn so the next turn (or agent) resumes without re-deriving.

label: Read the journal
summary: Page through the project's append-only journal (tool calls, model turns, consents, errors), filtered by day, kind or tool. Needs an open project.

label: Save a report
summary: Save a report a client composed (Markdown, HTML or plain text) to an absolute path the person chose. Only .md, .html, .htm or .txt files.

label: Write a readable report
summary: Turn the investigation (brief, plan, findings, hypotheses, handoff) and the evidence ledger into a readable report: what we looked at, what we found (each finding with its plain-English summary, confidence and cited evidence), open questions, and how it was done. format=markdown (default) or html. With an absolute path it writes the file (WRITES_FILESYSTEM); otherwise it returns the text.

label: List functions
summary: Every function the built-in engine found: entry, name, size, blocks, how it was found. Paged (offset/limit).

label: List segments
summary: Segments and sections with address ranges, file offsets, permissions and entropy.

label: List strings
summary: Printable strings (ASCII, UTF-8, UTF-16) in data sections with their addresses and how many places use them. Optional filters: one address, one section (`.rdata`); native_strings_find finds text. Paged.

label: List names
summary: Named addresses: your names, functions, data symbols and import slots. Optional single-address filter. Paged.

label: List documents
summary: Open targets (documents) with ids, kinds and which one is active.

label: List bookmarks
summary: Bookmarks you or an agent set on the active target.

label: Search functions
summary: Complete, deterministic search of function names (yours and the engine's) and imports (kind "import", e.g. CreateWindowExW). mode literal or regex; case-insensitive unless case_sensitive. Paged.

label: Search strings
summary: Complete, deterministic search of the program's strings. mode literal or regex; case-insensitive unless case_sensitive. Paged.

label: Read bytes
summary: Bytes at a virtual address as hex (default 256, at most 65536), never past the end of the section.

label: Address to file offset
summary: Map a virtual address to its offset in the original file (and the section holding it).

label: Cross-references
summary: References to an address (calls, jumps, data, strings, pointers, imports) and the references made from it. Defaults to the cursor. Paged.

label: Name at address
summary: The primary name at an address (your name first), or null.

label: Read comment
summary: The comment at an address, or null.

label: Read inline comment
summary: The inline comment at an address, or null.

label: Function info
summary: Entry, end, size, basic blocks, body ranges, call counts, jump tables and how the function was found.

label: Function assembly
summary: The function's assembly as one text listing (address, bytes, instruction, names).

label: What it calls
summary: Direct callees of a function, with resolved names and imports.

label: Who calls it
summary: Call sites that call (or tail-jump to) this function.

label: Function references
summary: Raw reference edges of a function: incoming (to its entry) or outgoing (from its code).

label: Decompile
summary: Structured pseudo-C from the built-in clean-room lifter: register-level variables, if/else and loops from the control-flow graph, resolved call names, inline string literals. Honest about its limits.

label: Function address
summary: Resolve a function name to its canonical entry address.

label: Function instructions
summary: Every instruction of a function with bytes, mnemonic, operands, flow and referenced addresses.

label: Which function is this in
summary: The function whose code contains an address.

label: Inspect instruction
summary: The instruction (or data) at an address: operands, flow, registers read and written, references, containing function.

label: Resolve a call
summary: Resolve the target(s) of one call or jump site: direct target, import, jump-table candidates, or unresolved.

label: Inspect data
summary: Best-effort typing of data at an address: string, pointer (to a function, string or data), pointer table, integer, or a requested type (u8…u64, i32, i64, f32, f64, pointer, cstring, utf16).

label: Name an address
summary: Give an address a name (an empty name clears yours). Names show everywhere: listings, assembly, pseudo-C, call graphs. Saved with the project.

label: Name many addresses
summary: Name several addresses at once; reports success per address.

label: Write comment
summary: Set the comment at an address (empty clears it) and read it back.

label: Write inline comment
summary: Set the inline (end-of-line) comment at an address (empty clears it) and read it back.

label: Bookmark
summary: Bookmark an address with an optional name.

label: Remove bookmark
summary: Remove the bookmark at an address.

label: Annotate function
summary: Rename a function and/or set its entry comment and inline comment in one step (empty strings clear), read them back, and return the refreshed function facts.

label: Cursor address
summary: The cursor address in the active document (set with native_cursor_goto or in the app).

label: Cursor function
summary: The function containing the cursor.

label: Current document
summary: The active document (open target).

label: Go to address
summary: Move the cursor to an address (must be mapped in the program).

label: Next address
summary: The address of the next instruction (in code) or next byte (in data) after an address (the cursor by default). Doesn't move the cursor.

label: Previous address
summary: The address of the previous instruction (in code) or previous byte (in data) before an address (the cursor by default). Doesn't move the cursor.

label: Overview
summary: One-page summary of a program: format, architecture, entry, segments, counts of functions/strings/imports/exports, libraries, hardening, toolchain hints. detail=summary keeps the full record and returns counts plus a reference to page with core_evidence_browse.

label: Function dossier
summary: Everything about one function in one record: facts, pseudo-C, assembly, basic blocks, callers, callees, references, strings, unresolved calls, API boundary and register value flow. Page through big facets with core_evidence_browse; detail=summary returns counts plus a reference first.

label: Call graph
summary: Callees (forward) or callers (backward) of a function, level by level, with edges and honest truncation.

label: Trace a feature
summary: Literal text → matching strings, functions and imports → the code that uses them → the functions involved.

label: Call path
summary: Shortest direct-call path from one function to another (forward or backward), with goal status and residual unknowns. Forward, the goal may also be an import (e.g. CreateWindowExW): the path ends at the call to it.

label: Decompile many
summary: Pseudo-C for several functions at once (up to 64); each item succeeds or fails on its own.

label: References to a name
summary: Exact name (function, data symbol or import) → its address and every reference to it. Gives reason name_not_found when nothing has that name.

label: API boundary
summary: The system and library APIs a function calls, grouped by purpose (files, network, processes, crypto…), plus internal calls, indirect calls and jump tables.

label: Value flow
summary: Register def-use graph of a function (which instruction's result each instruction reads), parameter uses and side effects, following callees to max_depth. Nodes are paged (offset/limit).

label: Objective-C classes
summary: Deduplicated Objective-C class and category names (with method counts), optionally filtered by a substring.

label: Objective-C protocols
summary: Objective-C protocols with their methods, plus Swift protocols from symbols.

label: Swift types
summary: Swift symbols grouped into classes, structs, enums, protocols, extensions and other, by type path and role (accessor, descriptor, method…).

label: Dispatch metadata
summary: Objective-C method dispatch (class, selector, implementation) and Swift dispatch-related symbols, up to max_records.

label: Trace a UI action
summary: UI action or selector (e.g. `saveDocument:`) → handlers (Objective-C methods, matching names, code using the string) → the static calls they make, bounded by max_depth/max_nodes/max_edges. Best effort; limits are listed.

label: Windows resources
summary: PE32/PE32+ resource tree (type → name → language) with SHA-256 of each item, icon groups, version information and the manifest. Built-in parser. Uses the active target unless path is given.

label: Binary layout
summary: Sections, segments (ELF program headers), symbols, relocations, linkage and hardening (NX, PIE, RELRO, canary, fortify, CFG…) of an ELF, PE or Mach-O file. detail=summary returns counts and keeps the complete record in the session.

label: Crash dump
summary: Read a Linux ELF core dump: the signal and its meaning, the faulting address, registers of each thread, the process name and arguments, mapped files, and which file the crash happened in.

label: DOS load image
summary: Check a DOS MZ or .COM program's load image: header, SHA-256 digests (file, header, load module), relocations, entry point and stack, with any inconsistencies.

label: What is this?
summary: Say what a file is in plain English (format, OS, architecture, language/toolchain hints such as Go, Rust, .NET, Electron, Flutter, Delphi, packers) and which toolsets and tools to use next. Uses the active target unless path is given.

label: Page through evidence
summary: View part of a stored (or inline) evidence record: the summary, one part, one row of a list, a page of a list's rows (optionally only the rows matching given field values, cut to chosen fields, with the field names listed), or a part of a function dossier (pseudocode, assembly, basic_blocks, callers, callees, flow_*…), with coverage and next_offset. Nothing is analysed again.

label: Mach-O structure
summary: Header, architecture slices, every load command (libraries with versions, run paths, UUID, build versions, encryption, code-signature range, entry point, segments) plus a page of imports and exports of a Mach-O file or an app bundle's executable. Built-in parser; uses the active target unless path is given.

label: Code signature
summary: Decode a Mach-O code signature: code directories (identifier, team id, flags, hash type, slot counts, cdhash), page and special-slot hashes re-computed and compared, requirements as text, entitlements, and whether a CMS signature is present. The CMS signature itself is not verified.

label: Property list
summary: Read a property list (XML or binary) as normalised JSON: a .plist file, an app bundle's Info.plist, or the Info.plist embedded in a Mach-O executable. Uses the active target unless path is given.

label: Architectures
summary: List the architecture slices of a thin or universal Mach-O (CPU type and subtype, offset, size, alignment, file type).

label: Demangle Swift symbols
summary: Turn mangled Swift symbol names into readable declarations, in order, each marked demangled, unchanged (not a Swift name) or invalid. Built-in demangler; no target needed.

label: Interface Builder documents
summary: Decode compiled nib and storyboard files (NIB archives and keyed-archive nibs; .nib, .storyboardc and whole app bundles) into object graphs: objects with classes and values, outlet and action connections, and the view hierarchy. Bounded by max_documents, max_objects and max_connections.

label: Keyed archive
summary: Read an NSKeyedArchiver property list: archiver, $top entries, the object table (paged) and the object graph below a root with references resolved (cycles and repeats become $ref).

label: Asset catalog
summary: Read a compiled asset catalog (Assets.car): BOM blocks and variables, catalog header, key format, facet names, appearances and a page of renditions (name, size, scale, pixel format, layout). Image pixels are not decoded.

label: Library resolution
summary: Follow how the dynamic linker would find every library an app bundle's programs load: @executable_path, @loader_path and @rpath chains, load-once, weak links and architecture slices, with outcomes resolved, system, unresolved or undetermined and findings such as skipped-rpath-entry. Never follows links out of the bundle.

label: Android app package
summary: Read an APK with built-in parsers: the manifest (package, versions, SDK levels, permissions, components with exported state and intent filters, application flags) decoded from binary XML, signing certificates (v1 PKCS#7 files and the v2/v3 signing block; signatures and content digests are verified, but not whether the certificate is one you trust), DEX files and native libraries per ABI.

label: Find Android classes
summary: Search the classes defined in an APK's DEX files (or a bare .dex) by name; an empty query lists every class. Paged (offset/limit).

label: Android class
summary: One class from an APK or .dex: superclass, interfaces, access flags, source file, annotations, fields and methods with Java-style signatures and overload indexes.

label: Android method bytecode
summary: A method's Dalvik bytecode as a smali-like listing with registers, resolved strings, types, fields and methods, branch targets, switch and array payloads and try/catch handlers (built-in decoder). With java_source=true and JADX installed, also attaches JADX's Java decompilation of the class.

label: Who uses this Android class?
summary: Every instruction in every DEX file of an APK that calls, reads, writes, creates, casts to or loads a class (or only calls one of its methods when method_name is given), with the calling method and code offset. Paged.

label: Android resources
summary: Decode resources.arsc with the built-in parser: packages, resource types and their configurations (locale, density, night mode, SDK…), every entry with typed values and style bags, string resources per locale; optionally decode compiled res/*.xml files to text. Paged.

label: Android app components
summary: The activities, activity aliases, services, receivers and providers an APK's manifest declares: exported state and where it comes from, permissions, intent filters (actions, categories, data), and a plain reachable_from_outside flag with who_can_reach (any_app, apps_with_permission or own_app_only), following the manifest's implicit export rules for its targetSdk. Filter by kind or reachable_only;

label: Is Apktool available?
summary: Report whether Apktool is installed (Settings path, managed engine store, then PATH) and its version. Craft Anything's built-in resource and manifest decoders need nothing installed; Apktool is optional.

label: Identify a Flutter build
summary: For an APK (or one Flutter library): which ABIs ship libapp.so/libflutter.so, the Dart snapshot version hash (null with candidates when libraries disagree), Dart versions and toolchains the binaries state, GNU build ids, and the size and SHA-256 of each libflutter.so. Built-in parser.

label: Inspect a Dart AOT snapshot
summary: Read a Flutter app's compiled Dart library (libapp.so, from an APK or directly): the dynamic symbols for the VM and isolate snapshots (from section headers or, for stripped images, PT_DYNAMIC with DT_HASH/DT_GNU_HASH), snapshot headers (kind, version hash, features), and a byte scan of the isolate snapshot for package:/dart: URIs and identifier tokens (tokens paged with offset/limit).

label: Check the JEB connection
summary: Connect to the user-run JEB MCP server set in Settings → Engines (jeb_url, loopback only), report its server information, upstream tools and client information. Never starts JEB.

label: Open a file in JEB
summary: Ask the user-run JEB MCP server to open an absolute file path as a project (upstream open_project). Not idempotent: JEB keeps the project open.

label: List JEB units
summary: List the units of the open JEB project (upstream list_units), optionally under parent_unit_path and filtered, one page at a time (index, count ≤ 100).

label: Decompile with JEB
summary: Ask JEB to decompile one type or method (upstream decompile_code_item) by item_address, optionally inside unit_path. The output is JEB's, recorded as external evidence.

label: Java archive overview
summary: Read a JAR or WAR with the built-in parser: the MANIFEST.MF attributes (main class, class-path, versions), the classes it defines grouped into a package tree, bundled dependencies (nested jars and native libraries), resources, and the class-file (Java) version(s) seen.

label: Find Java classes
summary: Search the classes (and optionally methods) defined in a JAR/WAR or a single .class by name; an empty query lists every class. Paged (offset/limit).

label: Java class
summary: One class from a JAR/WAR or a bare .class: its Java version, access flags, superclass, interfaces, source file, annotations, inner classes, and its fields and methods with Java-style signatures. With decompile=true, also a pseudo-Java skeleton of the class.

label: Java method bytecode and pseudo-Java
summary: A method's JVM bytecode as a disassembly listing with resolved constant-pool references (fields, methods, classes, string/number constants), branch targets, switch tables and the exception table, plus a best-effort structured pseudo-Java reconstruction (confidence Inferred). Paged over instructions.

label: Who uses this Java class?
summary: Every instruction in every class of a JAR/WAR (or a single .class) that calls, reads, writes, creates or casts to a class (or only calls one of its methods when method_name is given), with the calling method and bytecode offset. Paged.

label: Is adb available?
summary: Report whether Android platform-tools (adb) is installed (Settings path, the managed engine store, then PATH) and its version. Contacts no device. Needs nothing installed to answer.

label: Connected devices
summary: List phones and emulators attached to adb (`adb devices -l`): serial, connection state (device, unauthorized, offline…), product, model and transport id.

label: Device details
summary: Read a whitelist of device properties with `getprop` (manufacturer, brand, model, Android version and SDK level, security patch, CPU ABIs, build fingerprint/type). The full property set is parsed and counted; a bounded sample is attached.

label: Installed apps
summary: List installed package names with `pm list packages`. Scope all (default), third_party (-3) or system (-s).

label: Device log
summary: Read a bounded tail of the device log with `logcat -d` (dump and exit, never follow). count 1..10000 (default 500), buffer main|system|radio|events|crash (default main), optional pid filter. Lines are parsed into timestamp, pid, tid, level, tag and message.

label: App details on device
summary: Inspect one installed package with `dumpsys package <name>`: version name/code, userId, install and update times, data and code paths, declared and granted permissions. Key fields are parsed; a bounded raw tail is attached for the rest.

label: Running processes
summary: List running processes with `ps -A`, parsed into user, pid, ppid and name using the column header.

label: Device folder
summary: List a folder on the device with `ls -la` (the path is single-quoted for the device shell). Raw lines are kept; a best-effort parse of name, size and permissions is attached.

label: Device features
summary: List hardware and software features the device reports with `pm list features`.

label: System services
summary: List registered system services with `service list`: index, name and the AIDL interface each exposes.

label: Display info
summary: Read display state with `dumpsys display`. Key lines (display ids, real size, density, state) are surfaced; a bounded raw tail is attached.

label: Window / focus info
summary: Read window-manager state with `dumpsys window`. Focused window and app, and current activity lines are surfaced; a bounded raw tail is attached.

label: Read a setting
summary: Read one settings value with `settings get <namespace> <key>`. namespace system|secure|global; key is validated.

label: Find an app
summary: Find installed packages whose name contains a search term with `pm list packages <query>`.

label: Copy an app off the phone
summary: Copy an installed app's APK file(s) to a host folder: resolve paths with `pm path`, then `adb pull` each. output_directory must be absolute and must not exist yet; it is created fresh.

label: Copy a file off the phone
summary: Copy a file or folder from the device to a host folder with `adb pull`. output_directory must be absolute and fresh.

label: Screenshot
summary: Take a screenshot with `exec-out screencap -p` and write screen.png to a fresh host folder. output_directory must be absolute and must not exist yet.

label: Bug report
summary: Collect a full bug report with `adb bugreport` into a fresh host folder (this can take minutes). output_directory must be absolute and must not exist yet.

label: Copy a file to the phone
summary: Copy a host file to the device with `adb push`. local_path is an absolute host file; device_path is an absolute device path. With overwrite=false the tool refuses if the device path already exists. Changes the device.

label: Install an app
summary: Install an APK on the device with `adb install` (replace=true adds -r). apk_path is an absolute host file. Changes the device.

label: Remove an app
summary: Uninstall a package with `adb uninstall`. Changes the device.

label: Launch an app
summary: Launch a package's default activity with `monkey -p <pkg> -c android.intent.category.LAUNCHER 1`. Changes the device (starts an app).

label: Start an activity
summary: Start an activity with `am start`: action (validated), optional data_uri (single-quoted), optional component (pkg/.Activity), and as many as 16 extras, each a text, true/false, whole or decimal number value. Changes the device.

label: Force-stop an app
summary: Force-stop a package with `am force-stop`. Changes the device.

label: Frida devices
summary: List devices Frida can see with `frida-ls-devices` (local, usb, remote). Pass remote to query a remote frida-server; its auth is forwarded to the CLI and never returned.

label: Frida processes
summary: List processes and installed apps on the selected device with `frida-ps`. Give exactly one of device_id or remote.

label: Start a Frida session
summary: Begin a managed Frida session. mode=attach needs pid; mode=spawn needs program (absolute) and optional argv. Returns a session_id (held in memory) you pass to the other Frida tools. This records the session; code runs only when you load or resume a script.

label: Run a Frida script
summary: Load and run an instrumentation script in a session for a bounded window, capturing its console/send output. source_kind=inline with source, or source_kind=file with an absolute path. Executing a script runs foreign code, so this is consent-gated and changes the target.

label: Resume a Frida session
summary: Resume a spawned, paused session so the target runs. Executes foreign code (the target's own), so this is consent-gated.

label: Unload a Frida script
summary: Forget a loaded script in a session (record-keeping; the bounded CLI run that executed it has already ended).

label: Frida session status
summary: Report a managed session's state, its device/target, and the scripts run in it with their most recent captured messages.

label: Close a Frida session
summary: End a managed session and forget it. Never kills the target process.

label: One-shot instrumentation
summary: Attach to (or spawn) a target, run a script for duration_ms (0..60000, default 1000), capture its output, and detach — all in one call. Executes foreign code, so it is consent-gated and destructive.

label: Go program details
summary: Read a Go program (ELF, PE or Mach-O; pick a universal-binary slice with architecture): the build information block (Go version, main module, dependencies with versions, sums and replacements, build settings such as -ldflags, CGO_ENABLED, GOOS/GOARCH, vcs.revision) and the function name table (pclntab, Go 1.2–1.20+ layouts) with every function's name and entry address, paged, plus functions per pa

label: WebAssembly module
summary: Validate a WebAssembly module and list its sections, imports, exports, functions (signature, body size, name), memories, tables, globals, custom sections (names, producers, target features, source map URL), start function and data segments; optionally the text form (WAT), paged by characters; optionally scan JavaScript glue files for .wasm references and matching import names. Built-in parser.

label: Smart contract interface
summary: Find the public function selectors in EVM contract bytecode (raw or hex, from a file or inline): where the dispatcher sends each selector, whether the function refuses payments (CALLVALUE check), fallback/receive presence, binary-search dispatch, and the compiler metadata (solc/vyper version, IPFS/Swarm hash). Function names are not recoverable without an ABI. Never executes the code.

label: SQLite database contents
summary: Read a SQLite 3 database file without running any SQL: the header (page size, page count, text encoding, SQLite version that wrote it, WAL mode, freelist), the schema from sqlite_schema (tables, indexes, views and triggers with their CREATE statements and, for tables, parsed column names and types), per-table row counts (counted by walking the b-tree, bounded), and a page of rows from a named tabl

label: Solana program (sBPF)
summary: Inspect a Solana on-chain program or classic eBPF object (an ELF whose machine type is EM_BPF=247): the sBPF version (guessed from e_flags), sections (.text, .rodata, relocation tables), the dynamic symbol table, relocations with their R_BPF_* types, the syscalls it calls (resolved by the murmur3 hash of the helper name — sol_log_, sol_invoke_signed_*, …), the entrypoint, discovered functions with

label: Disassemble sBPF code
summary: Disassemble a range of eBPF / Solana sBPF bytecode into an instruction listing (address, mnemonic, operands, and resolved jump/call targets). Give a file (ELF with EM_BPF, or raw bytecode with encoding=raw) and an optional byte offset and length into the code. Built-in decoder; nothing is executed.

label: Firmware regions
summary: Signature scan of a firmware image or disk dump with the built-in engine: compression streams (gzip, zlib, xz, LZMA, bzip2, Zstandard, LZ4), archives (ZIP, tar, cpio, 7z, RAR, CAB), filesystems (squashfs, cramfs, romfs, JFFS2, UBI/UBIFS, ext2/3/4, FAT, ISO 9660), boot images (legacy boot-loader images, Android boot), device trees/FIT, executables (ELF, PE, Mach-O) and PEM blocks, each checked agai

label: Extract firmware
summary: Carve every recognised region of a firmware image into a new folder (output_directory must not exist yet), decompress gzip/zlib/xz/LZMA/bzip2/Zstandard streams, unpack ZIP, tar and cpio members and boot-image payloads, list and extract files from squashfs, cramfs, romfs, ext2/3/4 and (best-effort) JFFS2 filesystems, and repeat on what comes out up to max_depth levels. Bounded by max_output_bytes a

label: Files packed inside a file
summary: List the files carried inside one program or game file, recognised from its bytes (the reader used is in the result; `format` picks one when a file could be read several ways). Results give each member's path, size, how it's stored and what the file says it is, plus the facts of that kind of file, paged with offset/limit. `contains` keeps paths holding that text. For ordinary archives and app bund

label: Take out packed files
summary: Write files carried inside one program or game file into a new folder (output_directory must not exist yet; it is created). `paths` picks exact members, `contains` those holding some text; with neither, all of them. Never overwrites; a member whose path would leave the folder is skipped and named. Bounded by max_output_bytes and max_output_files. Writes manifest.json with every member's SHA-256 (u

label: Compiled Python file
summary: Read a CPython compiled file (.pyc): the Python version from its magic number, how it ties to its source (modification time and size, or a source hash), and, for Python 3.8 to 3.14, its compiled code: each module, class and function with its name, dotted name, source file, first line, argument counts, the names it uses and the text among its constants, paged with offset/limit, parents before child

label: List a game's archives
summary: Find the packed files in a game's folder (absolute path): Unreal paks (.pak, checked by their footer) and IoStore containers (.utoc), Unity serialized files (.assets, level<n>, globalgamemanagers) and bundles (.bundle, data.unity3d), and Godot packs (.pck, or carried at the end of a program, checked by their mark, with how many files each declares), each with its size and the tool that lists it. L

label: List an Unreal pak
summary: List what's inside an Unreal Engine .pak archive (absolute path): its version (1-11), mount point, compression methods, and every file with its size, stored size, compression and whether it's encrypted, paged and optionally filtered by a part of the path. Only the footer and index are read, so very large paks are fine. An encrypted index is reported, never guessed: listing it needs the game's own

label: List an Unreal IoStore container
summary: List what's inside an Unreal Engine IoStore container (absolute path of its .utoc table of contents, or of the .ucas beside it): its version, flags (compressed, encrypted, signed, indexed), compression methods, chunk and partition counts, and every named file with its size, stored size and compression, paged and optionally filtered by a part of the path. Unreal 5 games keep most of their assets th

label: List a Unity assets file
summary: List the objects in a Unity serialized file (absolute path: a .assets file, level<n>, globalgamemanagers, sharedassets<n>.assets in <Game>_Data) or in a bundle (.bundle, data.unity3d: every serialized file inside it, each object naming its `file`, or only `file`'s): the format version, Unity version, build platform, how many objects of each class (GameObject, Texture2D, AudioClip, MonoBehaviour…),

label: List a Unity bundle
summary: List the files inside a Unity asset bundle in the UnityFS format (absolute path: a .bundle, data.unity3d or Addressables file): its format, Unity version, block compression (LZMA, LZ4), and each file with its size, and for each serialized file inside, its Unity version, object count and objects by class. Only the blocks that hold those files' headers are decompressed. Paged and optionally filtered

label: Take an asset out of a Unity game
summary: Save one object of a Unity serialized file (absolute path of a .assets or level file, or of a bundle: then `file` picks the serialized file inside, the first by default) as a file anyone can open: a texture (Texture2D, by its path_id from game_unity_list) becomes a PNG at `output` (an absolute path that doesn't exist yet). Pixels are read inside the object or from the .resS file it streams from. F

label: Take a texture out of an Unreal game
summary: Save a texture of an Unreal Engine 4.26-4.27 game as a PNG, only when the person confirms they may unpack the game (permission: true; they made it or its rights holder allows it). path is the game's .pak (then `file` is the texture's .uasset path inside it, as game_pak_list shows it) or a .uasset already taken out, with its .uexp (and .ubulk) beside it. The largest mip the game ships is saved at `

label: Take files out of an Unreal pak
summary: Copy files out of an Unreal Engine .pak archive (absolute path). `file` is one file's path as game_pak_list shows it (any case) and `output` an absolute path that doesn't exist yet (its folders are made); the result has the size and SHA-256. A `file` ending in `/` (e.g. `Game/Content/UI/`) takes out every file under that folder into the folder `output`, keeping their layout, up to `limit` files pe

label: Read a Unity game's IL2CPP metadata
summary: Read a Unity IL2CPP global-metadata.dat (path: the file, or a game's folder, where it's found under *_Data/il2cpp_data/Metadata or Data/il2cpp_data/Metadata): the metadata version, its assemblies (images) and how many types, methods, fields and string literals it names. view picks a list to page: images, types (namespace, name, assembly, method and field counts), methods (name, declaring type, par

label: Work out what an installed app is built on
summary: Survey an installed app's folder (absolute path; a macOS .app or its Contents, a Windows or Linux install folder) when you don't know what it is. Walks the folder within max_entries and max_depth, following no links, running nothing and writing nothing, and reads only the first and last 4 KiB of the files that need a look, plus a search of up to 64 MiB of up to 4 main programs for Tauri's own text

label: .NET assembly overview
summary: Built-in ECMA-335 reader: PE/CLI header (runtime version, IL-only/32-bit/strong-name flags, entry point, ReadyToRun), metadata streams and table row counts, assembly identity, assembly and module references, manifest resources, forwarded types, assembly attributes (TargetFramework decoded) and a classification (runtime family, implementation, managed architecture). Uses the active target unless pa

label: .NET types and methods
summary: Types, fields, properties, events and methods of a .NET assembly with C#-like signatures; for each IL method body: header kind, max stack, locals, exception clauses, IL size, il_hash, an il_shape_hash that survives renames, call targets, field accesses and string literals (optionally the IL listing). Filter with type_names; paged by type (offset/limit).

label: .NET native calls
summary: Where a .NET assembly crosses into native code: P/Invoke (DllImport) rows with module, entry point, charset, calling convention, SetLastError, best-fit and PreserveSig; internal calls; native-code (mixed-mode) and runtime-implemented methods; UnmanagedCallersOnly and LibraryImport declarations; module references and vtable fixups.

label: Compare two .NET builds
summary: Compare the members of two assemblies (managed_members_list evidence or absolute paths) with tiered unique matching: identical IL and signature (survives renames), then type+name+signature, then the same structure. Reports unchanged, changed (body differs), renamed or moved, added, removed and ambiguous methods, plus added/removed types and fields.

label: Check .NET native calls
summary: Check each P/Invoke of a managed assembly (managed_native_calls_list evidence or a path) against the exports of native libraries (native_layout_show evidence or absolute paths): found, found as an A/W or stdcall-decorated variant, case mismatch, missing, or undetermined when the module wasn't supplied.

label: Check decompiled C#
summary: Check user-supplied C# (a file, a folder of .cs files, or text) against the assembly's member evidence: declarations matched, signature mismatches, members missing from the source, extra source members, compiler-implicit members, and missing/extra types. Declarations only, not behaviour.

label: .NET application graph
summary: Project a .NET assembly (managed evidence or a path) into an application graph: assembly, referenced assemblies, types, methods, external members, native modules and resources, joined by contains, references, inherits, calls and pinvoke edges. Bounded by max_nodes.

label: Run and watch a program
summary: Run a program under a terminal with a scripted timeline of typed input, resizes and signals, then record the terminal screen, exit, and (opt-in) which files changed. Values that change every run (process ids, loopback ports, 10 ms time buckets; optionally paths and literal patterns) are normalised so two runs compare. Bounded by time, output and files; the whole process group is killed on timeout

label: Compare two runs
summary: Compare two runtime_walkthrough_record evidence records dimension by dimension (terminal, exit, filesystem, events) and report what changed. Pure; no program is run.

label: What's at this address
summary: The name, containing function, comment, inline comment and bookmarks at one address in the active target. Each facet is a value or a clear 'unavailable' with a reason.

label: Compare two functions
summary: Compare two native_function_study evidence records: name, size, blocks, instructions, callee set and pseudo-code. Reports what changed.

label: Compare two evidence bundles
summary: Compare two exported evidence bundles (core_evidence_export files) and report which records were added, removed or changed, matched by operation and subject. Every record is checked against its own id, so one edited after export is reported, never counted as unchanged.

label: Summarise what changed
summary: Combine several comparison evidence records (app_function_versions_compare, core_archives_compare, runtime_captures_compare) into one summary of what changed and what stayed the same.

label: Find a call path
summary: Find a path of calls from a start address to a goal address over a call graph assembled from native_function_study evidence records.

label: Line up code and behaviour
summary: Correlate static comparisons (app_function_versions_compare/core_archives_compare) with runtime comparisons (runtime_captures_compare) through caller-supplied mappings, and report where they agree or disagree.

label: Check a rebuild claim
summary: Check a reconstruction specification: every expectation must cite evidence that exists and is intact. Reports which expectations are satisfied.

label: Read an app's screen
summary: Read the UI tree of a running app by its pid: every window's controls in order with their depth, role, title, identifier and value (macOS: the accessibility tree, optionally with a screenshot; Windows: UI Automation, also the class, position and size, and whether it's enabled; window_id picks one window by its handle). Password fields' values are never read; long values are cut at 500 characters.

label: Drive an app's screen
summary: Run a short scripted UI walkthrough against a running app by its pid and record its UI tree before and after the steps. Each step names an action and an element (its exact title or identifier). macOS: any accessibility action (e.g. AXPress). Windows (UI Automation): press (invoke, else toggle, select or expand), expand, collapse, toggle, select or focus; AXPress, AXShowMenu and AXRaise work too. E

label: Watch a Mac app's calls
summary: Launch a macOS program under lldb, set breakpoints on named functions and ObjC selectors, and record each hit with its argument registers. Bounded by duration and event count. macOS only.

label: Search for bytes
summary: Find every place a byte signature or a piece of text occurs in a file (an absolute path, or the active target). `pattern` is hex byte pairs with `??` for any byte (spaces optional, e.g. `48 8B ?? 24`); `text` is searched as UTF-8 and/or UTF-16LE. Matches are ordered by file offset and paged (offset/limit); for ELF, PE and Mach-O programs each match also carries its virtual address and containing s

label: Rust program details
summary: Identify a Rust program (ELF, PE or Mach-O, or any file) from its bytes: rustc version strings and the toolchain commit from /rustc/<commit>/ paths, the standard-library path layout, crates with versions from embedded Cargo paths (registry/src/<index>/<crate>-<version>/ and git checkouts), the program's own source paths left by panic locations, well-known panic messages, Rust symbol names (legacy

label: What a program imports
summary: The functions a program takes from other libraries, without analysing it. Windows programs: the import directory, the delay-load directory and bound imports, by name (with hint) or by ordinal, each saying which kind it is. ELF: the dynamic symbols with their needed version and library. Mach-O: bound symbols with how each library is linked. Libraries are summarised first, then rows are paged (offse

label: What a program exports
summary: The functions and data a program or library offers to others, without analysing it. Windows: the export directory with ordinals, names, ordinal-only entries and forwarders to other libraries. ELF: exported dynamic symbols with their versions. Mach-O: the export list. Paged (offset/limit); contains keeps rows whose name or forwarder holds that text. Uses the active target unless path is given.

label: Who signed this Windows program
summary: Read a Windows program's Authenticode signature block: each certificate table entry, the signer's subject, issuer, serial and validity dates, every embedded certificate, and the digest algorithm. Checks what the file alone can show: its hash against the signed hash, the signature against the embedded signer certificate, and how the embedded certificates link. Doesn't check whether Windows trusts t

summary: Read an AI model file's header: GGUF (versions 2 and 3) or safetensors. Architecture, name, quantization, approximate parameter count, metadata keys and values (long values shortened), and tensors with their types and shapes, paged (offset/limit). Reads at most max_header_bytes from the start of the file, so very large models are fine; tensor data is never read. Uses the active target unless path

label: Match functions between two builds
summary: Pair the functions of two builds of a program (two absolute paths) with the built-in engine. In order: unique names that aren't generated; identical bytes; bytes with addresses masked out; a structural fingerprint of block count, called names and referenced strings. Each pair says how it was matched, with what confidence, and what comparing the bodies found: a pair by name is still reported as cha

label: Write pseudo-C to a folder
summary: Write each function of the active target as pseudo-C to its own file in a folder, across as many runs as it takes: running again with the same folder skips what's done and continues, and a state file records the target's SHA-256 (another target is refused) and each finished function. Each call stops at max_functions or max_seconds and says how far it got. Files are written atomically. Uses the bui

label: Electron fuses
summary: Read the Electron fuse wire from a packaged Electron app without running it: pass the main executable (Windows .exe, Linux binary), the macOS .app bundle or Electron Framework binary, or the app's folder. Reports each wire's file offset, version and declared length, and every fuse by index with its name (RunAsNode, EnableCookieEncryption, EnableNodeOptionsEnvironmentVariable, EnableNodeCliInspectA

label: Compare WebAssembly interfaces
summary: Compare the imports and exports of two WebAssembly modules (absolute paths): each import by module and name, each export by name, with its kind (func, table, memory, global, tag) and exact signature (function parameter/result types, memory and table limits, global type). Lists what was added, removed or changed, paged, with counts including unchanged entries; scope picks imports, exports or both.

label: Packet capture overview
summary: Summarize a saved pcap or pcapng capture with the built-in decoder (nothing installed): format, interfaces and link types, packet and byte counts, time span, frames per protocol, busiest addresses, conversations (flows) with packets and bytes in each direction and the application protocols seen (paged), DNS questions and answers, HTTP/1.x requests (method, Host, target; credentials removed) and TL

label: Packet fields
summary: List decoded fields of individual packets in a saved pcap or pcapng capture, paged: frame number, time, link, protocol stack, addresses and ports, conversation (flow) id, IP TTL, TCP flags/sequence/window, UDP and ICMP details, DNS questions and answers, HTTP/1.x request or status line with Host, TLS ClientHello SNI/ALPN/versions. Filter by protocol (e.g. dns, tls, http, tcp, udp, icmp, ipv6, arp)

label: Wireshark tools check
summary: Check whether Wireshark's tshark is installed (Settings → Engines, the engine store, PATH, or the standard Wireshark folder) and which version it reports. Reads no capture. Optional: the built-in capture decoder works without it.

label: Capture inventories
summary: Inventories of a saved pcap or pcapng capture: packet count, protocol stacks, IPv4/IPv6 addresses with packet counts, DNS questions and the addresses answered for them, TLS server names (SNI) and HTTP request URIs (credentials removed), each with counts and limited to `limit` rows. Uses Wireshark's tshark when installed (engine=auto or tshark; full dissectors, run with a deadline and capped output

label: objdump output
summary: Run the installed objdump (GNU binutils or llvm-objdump) for one operation on a file (absolute path or the active target): file_headers, private_headers, section_headers, symbols, dynamic_symbols, relocations, dwarf (GNU only; debuginfod disabled), disassemble or disassemble_all (optionally between start_address and stop_address), or architectures (no file needed). Returns the raw text paged by li
