summary: Run one read-only Rizin command against a file (absolute path or the active target) with user settings and scripts disabled (`rizin -N -q -c <command> <file>`; the file is opened read-only). Commands are checked against an allow-list of read-only families: information (i…), printing and disassembly (p…, x…), analysis (a…), search (/…), seek (s…), flags (f…), comments (C…), types (t…) and help (?…)

label: ILSpy decompile
summary: Decompile a .NET assembly (absolute path or the active target) with the installed ILSpy command line (ilspycmd): operation decompile gives C# for the whole assembly, or for one type with type_name (`Namespace.Type`, nested types as `Outer+Inner`); il gives the whole assembly's IL; list_types lists its classes, interfaces, structs, delegates and enums. Its update check is turned off, so it never go

label: Start a GDB session
summary: Start GDB (machine-interface mode, no init files, auto-loaded scripts off, pagination off) with a program loaded (absolute path; optional core file and program arguments), or empty. The program is only loaded, not run. Returns a session_id for native_gdb_command_run, native_gdb_session_show and native_gdb_session_end, plus GDB's start-up messages. Sessions live in memory for this run; at most 4 at

label: GDB command
summary: Run one GDB command line in a session (for example `info functions`, `disassemble main`, `break main`, `run`, `bt`, `info registers`, `x/16xb $sp`) and return its console output, the result (done, running, error, exit), stop events (reason, frame) and any program output, waiting up to timeout_seconds for a started run to stop. Commands can run the program, call its functions or use GDB's shell and

label: GDB session status
summary: Show one GDB session (or all when session_id is omitted): whether GDB is alive, the last known program state (not started, stopped, running, exited), the last stop event, and any output that arrived since the last command.

label: Close a GDB session
summary: End a GDB session: ask GDB to exit, then stop it and anything it started (including a program it is debugging).

label: Start a Rizin debug session
summary: Start Rizin's debugger (user settings and scripts off, no prompt or colours) on a program (absolute path, optional arguments), which it starts stopped before its first instruction, or attach it to a running process by pid. Returns a session_id for native_rizin_session_command_run, native_rizin_session_show and native_rizin_session_end, plus Rizin's start-up messages. The program's own console outp

label: Rizin debug command
summary: Run one Rizin command line in a debug session (for example `dr` registers, `db main` breakpoint, `dc` continue, `ds` step, `dbt` backtrace, `dm` memory maps, `pd 10 @ rip`, `px 64 @ rsp`; chain with `;`) and return its output and any `ERROR:` lines, waiting up to timeout_seconds. A command still running at the deadline (a `dc` that never stops) keeps running and the next command waits for it. Visu

label: Rizin debug session status
summary: Show one Rizin debug session (or all when session_id is omitted): whether Rizin is alive, what it debugs, whether a command is still running, and any output that arrived since the last command.

label: Close a Rizin debug session
summary: End a Rizin debug session: ask Rizin to quit (which ends a program it started; an attached process is detached), then stop it and anything it started.

label: Decode a radio recording
summary: Decode a saved radio recording (absolute path or the active target) with rtl_433: I/Q samples (.cu8, .cs8, .cs16, .cf32) or demodulated AM/FM (.am.s16, .fm.s16), format and sample rate read from the file name (for example g001_433.92M_250k.cu8; 250 kHz when absent) unless sample_rate is given. Returns each decoded message (device model, id, channel and readings) paged with offset/limit, plus count

label: List radio decoders
summary: List the device protocols the installed rtl_433 can decode: number, name, and whether it runs by default (the others only run when asked for with decoders). Optional engine.

label: List shared Cutter sessions
summary: Find Cutter (or Rizin) sessions shared on this computer: each port given (default 9090) is asked what it has open (file, format, architecture). A session is shared by running `=h& 9090` in Cutter's console; nothing else is reachable.

label: Cutter command
summary: Run one read-only Rizin command in a shared Cutter session (port, default 9090) and return its text, paged by lines: information (i…), printing and disassembly (p…, x…), analysis (a…), search (/…), seek (s…), flags (f…), comments (C…), types (t…) and help (?…). Writes, shell escapes, scripts, debugging, pipes and chaining are refused. Analysis and seek commands change what the Cutter window shows,

label: Decompile Java with Vineflower
summary: Decompile a Java .class file or JAR (absolute path or the active target) to Java source with Vineflower, run as a program (its .jar with the configured Java, or a vineflower script; set its path in Settings → Engines). Without class: the decompiled source files with their line counts, paged with offset/limit (and the source itself when there is one file). With class (com.example.Foo or com/example

label: Start a rebuild
summary: Start building: a new project from a request and a target (a web address, an absolute path, or - for none), or a follow-up on an existing project. A coding agent studies, builds, checks and refines in the background; follow it with rebuild_status and project_show, answer its questions with project_inbox_answer. Up to `build.parallel` projects build at once (2 by default); more are queued and start

label: Rebuild status
summary: Whether a project's build is running in this session (or queued, and where), its status and note, the latest check, and how many questions are waiting.

label: Show a build's activity
summary: What a project's builds did, line by line, newest last: each stage, every command and file the builder touched and how it ended, what it said, and what programs printed outside the conversation. Secrets are hidden. Works while a build runs and after. `limit` lines (200 by default, at most 2000), `offset` lines back from the newest.

label: Add to a running build
summary: Tell a running build something more; the agent reads it at its next step. With no build running, start a follow-up with rebuild_start instead.

label: Take back a note
summary: Take back a note given with rebuild_note (by the id it returned) while the agent hasn't read it yet; it returns the note's text. Once the agent has read it, it can't be taken back.

label: Stop a rebuild
summary: Pause a project's running build. Its work so far is kept; a follow-up continues it.

label: Ask about a build
summary: Ask a question about a project's build ("where are the latest files?", "why this engine?") without starting a build or a round, and without changing anything. Claude Code answers from a copy of the builder's own session, which isn't kept, reading files only (none in Clean room); an AI with an API key answers with the tools that change nothing. Other coding agents are refused. Safe while a build ru

label: List questions about a build
summary: The questions asked about a project's build and their answers, oldest first (the newest 200).

label: Check my build
summary: For the builder: test the project's current build against the original now, with the same checks Craft Anything runs after each turn (a website's likeness at each width with the padding, colour, font and layout differences; an app's or game's picture against the original's; whether it builds; the mechanics sheet; credits). The project's running build answers it, so the builder can fix what it list

label: Is an asset key set up?
summary: Whether each asset provider (fal.ai today) has a key for generated pictures and 3D models, stored or in its environment variable. `stored` answers for `provider` (default fal). Keys themselves are never shown.

label: Save an asset key
summary: Store an asset provider's key (`provider`, default fal) for generated pictures and 3D models in the system keychain (or the private key file). It's never shown again or written to logs.

label: Remove an asset key
summary: Remove an asset provider's stored key (`provider`, default fal).

label: Plan connecting agent apps
summary: What connecting Craft Anything to coding-agent apps (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor…) would change: each config file, the lines that change, and the skill files. Writes nothing.

label: Connect agent apps
summary: Connect Craft Anything to coding-agent apps: register its MCP server in their config files (backing each up first) and install the skill. Changes other apps' files, so it asks first.

label: Check the setup
summary: Check the install, each agent app's registration, engines, and that the MCP server answers.

label: Disconnect agent apps
summary: Remove Craft Anything's entries and skill from every agent app's config. Changes other apps' files, so it asks first.
